analysis.title: Canadian National Railway Co. (CNR.TO): 3Q26 EPS Beat, FY26 EPS Growth Guide Maintained at MSD-HSD (vs ~HSD Consensus)
key_insights: CN (CNI, GS rating Sell) reported 3Q26 adjusted EPS of C$2.16 versus C$2.11 GSe and C$2.09 FactSet consensus. Reported EPS was $2.00 after $14M of advisory costs tied to rail consolidation and $118M of asset impairment.
Adjusted operating ratio (OR) was 61.0% versus the 61.7% GSe forecast and 61.6% consensus, and 61.4% in 3Q25. Revenue was about 2% above both GSe and consensus, so EBIT came in about 4% above both.

Below-forecast purchased services and casualty/other expenses were the main drivers of the OR beat (combined about 1,300bps below forecast). They were partly offset by fuel expense about 900bps above forecast.
Revenue per carload rose 15% YoY versus a 13% forecast, while carloads fell 0.3% YoY versus a 0.1% decline forecast. Non-freight revenue was $197M versus $180M GSe, which also lifted total revenue.

Fuel was a 60bps headwind to OR in 3Q, versus 210bps in 2Q and 80bps in 1Q. EPS got a 14 cent benefit from fuel in the quarter after a 4 cent drag in 1H. If fuel prices hold, CN expects an EPS tailwind of about 10 cents in 4Q with 100-150bps of OR headwind.

FY26 guidance is maintained: EPS growth up mid-single to high-single digits YoY on low-single-digit revenue-ton-mile growth. Commentary pointed to the higher end of the EPS range. Consensus was at +7% EPS growth and GS at +8% coming into the print.

3Q carloads were roughly flat. Intermodal fell about 6% and coal about 10% (coal production problems, wildfire and overseas weather disruption to intermodal). Grain rose 10%, and auto, metals and petroleum/chemicals were up mid-to-high single digits.

Early 4Q trends are weaker. Total carloads are tracking down about 3% YoY (revenue-ton-miles -1%), below GS's roughly flat forecast. Coal is -15%, intermodal -4%, auto -3%, and grain and metals each about -1%. Forest and petroleum/chemicals are each +4%. CN expects grain and fertilizer growth to moderate as it laps last year's record.

CN has over 200 stored locomotives and spare network capacity, including in the west. It can handle added volume without adding resources at the same rate. YTD revenue-ton-miles are tracking up about 4%, slightly above the low-single-digit target.

GS FY26/27/28 EPS estimates move to C$8.23/C$9.20/C$10.20 from C$8.15/C$9.15/C$10.15. The FY26 estimate implies EPS +9% YoY. Changes reflect the higher 3Q base, yield trajectory and minor margin adjustments for seasonality and QTD carload trends.

GS price targets rise to C$187 (CNR.TO) and $136 (CNI), from C$182 and $132. They use an unchanged multiple of about 19x on Q5-Q8E EPS of C$9.98 and a USD/CAD rate of 1.38. Implied upside is 7.7% on CNR.TO (C$173.68) and 9.6% on CNI ($124.06).

GS keeps a Sell on CN and prefers trucking (LTL/TL) over rails, near the end of a long freight recession with trucking margins closer to a bottom. It says CN is delivering on earnings and expects solid incremental margins as volumes recover.

UNP announced an agreement with CN tied to the proposed UP/NS merger. Subject to regulatory approval, CN gains certain trackage rights and terminal stakes, with Midwest expansion and competitive access, in exchange for not opposing the merger and working through the Surface Transportation Board process. Management is positive about longer length of haul and more access into Mexico.
CFO Ghislain Houle will retire and be succeeded by Jamie Lockwood, currently VP Investor Relations, who joined CN in 2008.

market_movers.rationale: Sell reiterated with the target raised from $132 after a 3Q beat and slightly higher estimates. GS favors trucking over rails and sees limited upside to the shares.

sector_views.rationale: GS shifted recommendations toward trucking over rails near the end of a freight recession. It sees more earnings torque there as margins near a bottom.
Rails are seen as the more defensive group with less torque. CN is executing well, but GS has CN at Sell and expects grain-related carload headwinds after a strong crop year.

earnings_insights: CN 3Q26 adjusted EPS C$2.16 (reported 10/30) versus GSe C$2.11 and FactSet consensus C$2.09. Reported EPS of $2.00 includes $14M of advisory costs and $118M of asset impairment.

3Q26 adjusted OR 61.0% reported versus GSe 61.7% and consensus 61.6%. EBIT C$1,862M reported versus GSe C$1,795M and consensus C$1,791M. Revenue C$4,771M reported versus GSe C$4,682M and consensus C$4,665M.
Recurring net income C$1,307M reported versus GSe C$1,270M and consensus C$1,260M.

FY26 EPS guide: up mid-single to high-single digits YoY, tracking toward the higher end, on low-single-digit revenue-ton-mile growth. GS FY26E EPS C$8.23 (prior C$8.15), FY27E C$9.20 (prior C$9.15), FY28E C$10.20 (prior C$10.15).
GS quarterly EPS forecasts: 4Q26E C$2.20, 1Q27E C$2.02, 2Q27E C$2.34.
GS FY26E revenue C$18,892M (prior C$18,742M), EBITDA C$9,046M and EBIT C$7,083M. FY25 revenue was C$17,303M.
3Q freight revenue rose 14.7% YoY versus a 12.8% GSe forecast. Coal revenue +5.5% versus -1.5% GSe, and automotive +29.2% versus +23.0% GSe.
risk_factors: Early 4Q carloads tracking down about 3% YoY, below GS's flat forecast, with coal at -15%.
Grain and fertilizer growth expected to moderate as CN laps last year's record, with possible grain-related carload headwinds despite a very strong crop year.
Intermodal and coal weakness from production problems and wildfire and weather disruption.
Fuel price swings: a 60bps OR headwind in 3Q, and a potential 100-150bps OR headwind in 4Q if prices hold.
Tariff-related volume headwinds and a still-soft freight economy.

Upside risks to GS's Sell: volume and yield outperformance, a grain harvest stronger than the long-run average, margin expansion beyond other rails, and renewed US supply chain congestion or worse US rail service metrics.

tension_points.bull_case: CN beat 3Q EPS and OR, maintained an MSD-HSD EPS growth guide tracking to the high end, has over 200 stored locomotives for operating leverage, and GS expects solid incremental margins as volumes recover.
tension_points.bear_case: Early 4Q carloads are tracking down about 3% YoY with coal -15%, intermodal -4% and auto -3%. Grain growth is expected to moderate against last year's record, and GS prefers trucking over rails with CN at Sell.
tension_points.what_invalidates: GS lists upside risks to its Sell: volume and yield outperformance, a grain harvest stronger than the long-run average, margin expansion beyond other rails, and worse US rail service metrics for competitors.
